title: Android implementation guide
lead: Adapt PlayerConfig, SourceConfig and the UI in the existing Kotlin app. Follow settings through the screen, SDK code and observed result, then compare touch-driven mobile controls with Android TV remote input.

blocks.text: Integrate the Android player
blocks.summary: Create the SDK Player and connect its PlayerView to the existing Compose screen, keeping app helpers and SDK objects distinct.

blocks.text: This chapter follows the existing Kotlin app in apps/android. Android phones and tablets, Android TV, and Android-based Fire TV use that Android app and SDK. Fire TV running Vega OS uses the separate Vega implementation guide. Start with a working on-demand (VOD) source, then change one setting at a time and compare the applied Kotlin code with the observed playback.

The app uses Bitmovin Player Android 3.171.0+jason. This artifact relocates its Media3 dependency to coexist with the bundled advertising dependency. Use the Player, UI, Analytics and MediaSession combination in app/build.gradle.kts.

rows: Player / PlayerConfig
Playback engine and settings fixed when it is created.
PlayerSettings.toPlayerConfig and PlayerController.createPlayer.

A media item: URL, format, start position, tracks and content protection.

blocks.title: Create the SDK Player from fresh configuration

blocks.text: PlayerController, PlayerSettings, ApiOverrides and ApiNativeFactories are Player Lab helpers. They prepare fresh PlayerConfig, overrides and Android resources before calling the SDK constructor Player(context, prepared.config, analytics.playerConfig(...)). Include the helpers when reusing this code, or build those SDK objects in your own integration.

MainActivity creates the controller in onCreate, installs the Compose screen and loads the first catalog source. The controller owns the Player across ordinary Compose recomposition and UI-mode changes; creating a new Player inside every composable render would reset playback and leave extra instances to release. A source load is observed through Source and Player events, rather than treating a load call as proof that playback has started.
PlayerConfig and SourceConfig
blocks.summary: Build fresh PlayerConfig and SourceConfig objects, compare draft and applied values, and add typed SDK overrides or callbacks.

blocks.text: PlayerDraft and SourceDraft validate and normalize app inputs. The SDK receives fresh PlayerConfig and SourceConfig objects. Drafts remain separate from applied settings, with independent Source and Player apply actions.
Creation-time player settings

blocks.title: Construct PlayerConfig from the standard form

blocks.text: PlaybackConfig sets startup autoplay, mute and player-wide audio-language priority. BufferConfig sets buffered media targets. AdaptationConfig controls automatic quality selection and preloading. NetworkConfig supplies the retry policy. These nested SDK settings are fixed when the Player is created: do not mutate an existing PlayerConfig to change an active player. Use the runtime API for an immediate action, or build a new Player when changing creation-time configuration.

rows: Autoplay / Start muted
PlaybackConfig.isAutoplayEnabled / isMuted; both default off
Enable only mute and apply: playback waits for Play and starts muted. These are separate from runtime controls.
SDK live time shifting
PlaybackConfig.isTimeShiftEnabled; default on
Player creation-time setting. More → Playback options → Enable live rewind controls is a separate app preference and does not change VOD behavior.
Buffer
BufferConfig.startupThreshold / restartThreshold; BufferMediaTypeConfig.forwardDuration; defaults 2.5/5/50 seconds
Try 1/2/10 seconds and compare code and loading/rebuffer behavior on the same source.
Maximum automatic video bitrate
AdaptationConfig.maxSelectableVideoBitrate; whole bit/s, blank = Int.MAX_VALUE (2147483647), no cap
Try 1500000. This caps automatic selection; manual selection can choose higher qualities.
Preload / Allow rebuffering
AdaptationConfig.preload / isRebufferingAllowed; both default on
Control preloading and rebuffering separately.
Live quality / stability balance
AdaptationConfig.qualityStabilityBalance; 0–1, default 0.5
Applies near the live edge. Values toward 1 favor stability; toward 0 favor quality. Try 0.8 on live, separately from VOD.
Player audio priority
PlaybackConfig.preferredAudioLanguages
Try de, en. A nonempty source priority list takes precedence.
HTTP retry delays
RetryHttpRequestConfig.Retry; finite nonnegative seconds
0, 0.25, 2 allows one retry per value. Blank uses LinearIncreasingBackoffRetry; none disables retries.

blocks.text: Startup and Restart are buffered media duration needed to start or resume, not wall-clock delays. The standard editor requires nonnegative thresholds no greater than forward buffer minus 0.5 seconds, and a forward buffer of at least 0.5 seconds. Numeric fields reject non-finite values.
A smaller forward buffer retains less media but leaves less room for network variation. Memory also depends on bitrate and the decoder.

The standard retry field does not alter callbacks, request credentials or DRM-license renewal retries; use their separate SDK settings. Compare retries on a source you control where request failures can be reproduced.

blocks.caption: Settings with Player and Autoplay selected. Apply player builds a new PlayerConfig and recreates the player. The selected field is shown directly above the fixed actions.

blocks.text: Source-specific settings and loading

blocks.title: Build a new SourceConfig for each load

blocks.text: The normal path is SourceConfig(url, type). The alternative constructors in the excerpt support the app’s legacy MediaSource comparison and are not necessary for a new integration. SourceSettings adds title, poster, start options, live latency, preferred audio and one external WebVTT subtitle track. WebVTT is a text subtitle format with timed cues. Blank optional fields leave the corresponding SDK option unset.

rows: URL and type
SourceConfig(url, SourceType)
Use an HTTP(S) URL and DASH/HLS/Smooth/Progressive. HTTP depends on device cleartext policy. Selecting a type does not convert media.
Title and poster
SourceConfig.title / posterSource / isPosterPersistent
Title and poster URL are optional; blank uses SDK defaults. Persistent poster is also configurable.
Start position
SourceOptions(startOffset, startOffsetTimelineReference)
Seconds, blank = SDK default. The default reference is Start for VOD and End for live. Try 5 seconds/Start; the SDK corrects out-of-range offsets.
Source audio priority
SourceConfig.preferredAudioLanguages
A nonempty list overrides Player priority; blank inherits it. No match keeps the SDK default track.
External WebVTT subtitles
SourceConfig.subtitleTracks with SubtitleTrack
The standard form adds one track. isDefault is metadata; enable the track in the subtitle menu after reloading.
Live target latency
SourceLiveConfig.targetLatency
Finite seconds; blank keeps liveConfig = null and SDK defaults. VOD ignores it.

blocks.text: Audio lists trim whitespace and remove duplicates without regard to case while preserving priority. External subtitles use an HTTP(S) WebVTT URL with optional label/language. Clear metadata when removing the URL; in-stream subtitles remain available.

Live target latency changes the SDK’s definition of the live edge and asks it to approach the target while avoiding stalls. It applies on source reload and survives Player recreation. It guarantees neither end-to-end latency nor a seek-completion or convergence deadline. See test results for the checked environments.

SourceConfig describes the media; Source is the SDK’s media-item object. After applying source overrides, loadCurrentSource constructs Source instances and registers their events. The excerpts show the SDK construction and load calls: owner is the current Player, and only an explicit playlist override uses PlaylistConfig. Loading a new Source does not itself require a new Player.

blocks.title: Create SDK Source objects
Load a single source or configured playlist

items: Apply source loads a new Source on the same Player, excluding unapplied Player edits. Apply player creates a new Player with the applied source, excluding unapplied Source edits.
Recreation retains source metadata/options, UI mode, app rewind preference and the event log. It follows the start offset and Autoplay without restoring the old playback position.
Reset draft changes only the draft. A preset replaces source fields/options while retaining Player settings. Switching fields or tabs retains drafts.
Inspect standard PlayerConfig/SourceConfig/PlayerViewConfig alongside Code → SDK overrides. Standard code does not include every additional override.

blocks.caption: Applied Kotlin configuration in Code. The actual license is replaced with a placeholder. Additional SDK overrides have their own code display.

blocks.text: Additional typed settings and callbacks

SDK overrides have three distinct states: edited input, staged changes and applied configuration. Stage validates and retains the selected input; Apply SDK sends the complete staged set by recreating the Player. Remove stages a removal, and Apply restores the standard form value or SDK default. Code excludes uncommitted drafts. Apply copied override assignments to fresh mutable playerConfig/playerViewConfig objects before constructing Player, Source and PlayerView.

Overrides take precedence over basic settings. Lists such as SourceConfig.subtitleTracks and PlaylistConfig.sources construct typed objects from elements and child fields. Subtitle default metadata does not enable captions; playlist preloading can increase network and memory use.

Companion ad containers, SimpleCache and Cronet create real Android objects. Prepare the Google Play services Cronet provider before applying it. Cache settings read existing data; ordinary playback does not populate that cache.

Save startup-only settings such as DebugConfig.isLoggingEnabled, then fully restart the app. Current process values and saved next-launch values are separate. Keep debug logs local because they may contain confidential information.

Supported SDK callbacks accept a JavaScript function body. The app evaluates plain input/output values and adapts the result to the SDK callback. For LabelingConfig.videoQualityLabeler, return a label using height/bitrate, open the quality menu, then inspect calls in More → Diagnostics.

Execution is bounded, with no Java, Android or Player object access. Invalid results or exhausted budgets use the documented fallback. Zero calls means the SDK has not invoked that path. The interpreter is an app helper.
Change the player UI and screen layout
blocks.summary: Change WebView-based player controls and Compose layout, package custom UI resources, and account for TV focus and input.

blocks.text: The app has two UI layers. PlayerView renders native video and hosts the SDK’s HTML/JavaScript controls in a WebView, an Android view for web content. Compose renders the preview selectors, workspace navigation and editors. Editing Compose typography changes those app controls; it does not change the HTML player’s fonts. Editing shared player CSS changes the overlaid controls; it does not change Compose buttons.

blocks.title: Choose mobile or TV controls while retaining custom themes

blocks.text: Theme passes Default, Sports, Live or Cinema to the helper above. To add a custom UI, build it in packages/ui-shared/src/liveUi.ts, register its factory in global.ts and select it through UiMode or the Custom factory override. The mobile/TV table below lists the default variants.

rows: Colors and fonts
Keep the base CSS and set UiConfig.WebUi.supplementalCssLocation to an additional CSS asset.
Inspect the overlaid controls; the Compose form is unchanged. Include the CSS in the APK.
Buttons and their order
Edit the shared factory’s components array and its CSS classes, then rebuild the shared UI.
Switch to that custom UI. A CSS change alone does not create a new functional control.
Extra UI options
Use UiConfig.WebUi.customOptions for serialized UIConfig options. The separate UiConfig.WebUi.playbackSpeedSelectionEnabled property controls speed choices.
Check that the selected factory supports the option and that the menu changes.
Hide overlaid controls
Run PlayerView.isUiVisible with visible=false in APIs.
Controls hide immediately. Restore true; the app’s outer Compose controls remain available.
Scale video inside its bounds
Use PlayerViewConfig.scalingMode at view creation, or runtime PlayerView.scalingMode.
Fit preserves the whole image; choose other supported modes to compare cropping or stretching.
Change player bounds
Edit PlayerWorkspace layout and PlayerPreview in PlayerWorkspace.kt. Phones use a bounded preview; wide landscapes place it beside the workspace.
Keep the same PlayerView during presentation changes. TV controls use overscan-safe outer margins; fullscreen video fills its surface.

blocks.text: Edit PlayerViewConfig.uiConfig and UiConfig.WebUi in SDK overrides. TvUi/SmallScreenUi and a Custom factory are mutually exclusive. Remove WebUi field overrides before using UiConfig.Disabled.
Apply SDK recreates the Player even for view settings. Compose-only controls must call Player.play/pause/seek and subscribe to playback state. Disabling Web UI does not create those controls.

blocks.title: Embed PlayerView in the existing Compose screen

blocks.text: AndroidView connects Compose to a conventional Android View. Its key contains the Player instance, selected UI, actual television mode and view revision. Replacing PlayerView detaches and releases the old view; changing only Theme retains the Player and source. PlayerTouchHost keeps a gesture that starts inside the player with that view until it ends or is cancelled. Touch interception does not define remote focus: the Compose controls and the SDK WebView have separate focus behavior.

pnpm --filter @showcase/ui-shared build
bash scripts/sync-webui-bundle.sh
cd apps/android
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug

Run these commands from the repository root after changing the shared UI, then install the rebuilt APK. The synchronization step copies built assets; changing source files without building and reinstalling leaves the old UI in the app. For a CSS-only experiment, supplementalCssLocation adds to the base CSS, whereas cssLocation replaces the stylesheet entry point.
Android TV and Android-based Fire TV

Mobile and TV use the same Android SDK and playback owner in this sample, with different input and presentation rules. Player Lab reads Configuration.UI_MODE_TYPE_TELEVISION from the actual device configuration. It keeps the existing Compose workspace, adds 48 dp horizontal and 27 dp vertical safe margins, increases app text sizes and outlines focused selectors, tabs and switches. A wide phone or tablet remains a mobile device. Fullscreen video is not inset to the workspace margins.

blocks.title: Read the device mode for input presentation

rows: App workspace (Compose)
Touch and software-keyboard input; Source and Theme above the editor in portrait.
The shared settings workspace uses safe margins, larger text and visible directional focus while retaining the same drafts.
SDK controls inside PlayerView
Default uses the SDK SmallScreenUi for touch-oriented controls. This is the PlayerViewConfig() default; the SDK does not automatically select TvUi.
Default explicitly creates WebUi(variant = TvUi, focusUiOnInitialization = true), which selects UIFactory.buildTvUI and starts WebView spatial navigation.
Custom Sports, Live and Cinema
Uses the selected shared Custom factory.
Keeps the same Custom factory. Check or build its remote navigation separately; choosing a custom theme does not apply TvUi.
Values and player ownership
Drafts remain separate from applied configuration.
The same rule: changing a selection, focus or app language does not apply drafts or replace the Player. Theme replaces the view; Apply player recreates the Player.

blocks.text: This sample adapts existing androidx.compose.material3 controls. A dedicated TV destination can use androidx.tv.material3.Button and other components from androidx.tv:tv-material. TV and mobile have separate MaterialTheme types; keep each surface consistent while reusing Player ownership and settings state.

Every control needs a reachable D-pad target, visible focus and a distinct selected state. Restore focus after selectors/content changes and test movement between Compose and the SDK WebView. focusUiOnInitialization requests focus at WebView initialization; the host manages broader restoration.

When using SDK overrides to compare a UI variant, remove a custom-factory override, stage UiConfig.WebUi.variant = TvUi and also stage focusUiOnInitialization = true. A data-class copy from SmallScreenUi can retain its previous false focus value. Remove or reset the overrides afterward. The Theme picker and an explicit SDK override are separate inputs; applied code shows the standard view config and the override assignments separately.

TV Back uses public Android ViewGroup.dispatchKeyEvent to reach the focused SDK view. When the current preview has focus outside fullscreen/PiP, the host sends KEYCODE_ESCAPE ACTION_DOWN and ACTION_UP, then returns focus to Source. Key-up closes and resets the SDK menu, including nested quality pages.
Native dialogs and the on-screen keyboard handle Back in their own windows first. Other D-pad and Select events follow normal focus dispatch.

blocks.title: Send Escape press and release before returning native focus
blocks.text:
// The SDK TV UI closes and resets its menu on Escape key-up. Deliver both before leaving its view.
                view.dispatchKeyEvent(KeyEvent(KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN, KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ESCAPE))
                view.dispatchKeyEvent(KeyEvent(KeyEvent.ACTION_UP, KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ESCAPE))
                view.clearFocus()
                controller.requestWorkspaceFocus()
On TV, ConfigField keyboard Done and workspace Done share a path: close the on-screen keyboard, wait for selectors to return, then focus Source. Back returns to the selector.

Search dialogs read WindowInsets.isImeVisible and return to the first match or Close. A floating TV keyboard can be visible with zero inset height. Dismissal or changes to query, selection or matches cancel the return. Workspace restoration also checks that the editing scope and Player/view owners are still current.
Phones retain normal keyboard completion; record-editor dialogs keep focus within their own window. Hardware-keyboard editing without an on-screen keyboard retains normal caret and arrow behavior.

Dedicated MEDIA_PLAY_PAUSE, MEDIA_PLAY and MEDIA_PAUSE keys are separate from D-pad navigation. An active SDK MediaSession keeps the Android system route. Without one, the TV host calls the current Player on the first ACTION_DOWN and consumes the same press’s repeats and ACTION_UP, so a single press does not toggle twice. This policy does not create a MediaSession or change the current Player or Source.

items: Use only the TV remote: reach Source, Theme, workspace tabs, the selected Setting and fixed Apply or Run actions. Check that focus is visible and selected values stay distinguishable.
Open a selection dialog, move through its options, choose one and open it again. Back should dismiss the dialog before leaving the screen; its selected value and unapplied drafts must remain intact.

In Default, test the SDK TV playback controls, timeline and settings with the D-pad and Select. Test focus movement between native app controls and the SDK WebView, plus Back while a player menu or fullscreen view is open.
Check readability from the intended viewing distance and keep important app controls inside the safe area. Verify ads, track menus and lifecycle transitions on the intended hardware.

blocks.title: Recorded TV environment and platform services
blocks.text: The normal app was checked on a 1920 × 1080 Android TV API 36 emulator: SDK TvUi, native selection/text input, SDK-menu Back, media keys with MediaSession on/off, and retained drafts/playback owners. TV captures use that environment.

Check viewing distance, safe margins and hardware decoders separately on physical Android TV/Fire TV. Google Play services-dependent options, including the selected Cronet provider, also need Fire TV checks. Vega OS uses the separate Vega app.
Playback features, events and lifecycle
blocks.summary: Use runtime commands with SDK state and events, integrate system media and offline playback, and release views and players with their owners.

blocks.text: Runtime commands, state and events

Runtime APIs operate on the current Player, Source or attached PlayerView. Refresh reads current SDK values; Events records counts and timestamps. Check completion events and state alongside the call result for asynchronous work.

rows: Call result
The SDK return value, or a short submission receipt for a command returning Unit.
A submitted command can still be asynchronous. Check the relevant completion event and SDK state before judging its media effect.
Value at last refresh
One actual SDK read at Refresh SDK state.
Keys and opaque request/configuration objects are excluded. Displayed text and lists are bounded; refresh again after the SDK changes.
This app session
Recorded event counts and latest SDK timestamps for the current app session.
Zero means no recorded occurrence. Timestamps are milliseconds since the Unix epoch. History can include events from before the latest API call; payloads, headers and keys are excluded.
Special state
Ad values need an active ad or selected SSAI test object. Vector3 reads the last moveViewingDirection input.
activeAdBreak and activeLinearAd read actual SDK state. Do not confuse a stored test input with current playback state.

blocks.text: PlayerView on/next/off receives UI events such as FullscreenEnter/Exit. Playback/source events are recorded on Player and Source, without forwarding them through view subscriptions.

PlaylistApi.seek time is SeekTarget.offset in seconds. Start uses nonnegative offsets, End nonpositive offsets; the SDK corrects out-of-range targets to boundaries. null uses the source default; useSeekTarget=false passes a null target.

The VR renderer replaces PlayerView with a decoder-backed OpenGL surface and restores it when disabled. It needs a compatible source VR content type. Callbacks retire with the renderer; app:vr-renderer exposes decoded-frame and execution observations.
Update scripts receive {delta, viewingDirection} and return {text?, move?: {phi,x,y}} or null. delta is seconds. everyFrames limits script frequency while the SDK frame clock follows display updates.

blocks.caption: State reads the selected SDK value, Player.currentTime in this example. Refresh is a point-in-time read, separate from submitting a command.

blocks.title: Register and remove the same guarded SDK listener

blocks.text: The helper subscribes with owner.on(type, guarded) and retains the same guarded function for owner.off. It also checks that the event belongs to the current Player and generation, so a retired Player cannot update the replacement screen. Source events are observed on Source; view subscriptions are for PlayerView UI events such as fullscreen. In a new integration, retain listener identity for removal and release subscriptions with their owner.
Playback features and system integration

rows: Audio and subtitles
Source and Player fields in Settings → Configuration; track methods in APIs.
Use matching content. Reload source preferences, then enable subtitles or choose tracks in the player menu.
Live rewind
Player.timeShift, maxTimeShift and the app’s window clamping.
Use a live source with an available window. Compare timeShift/TimeShifted and return to live with timeShift(0.0).
Fullscreen and picture-in-picture
Host handlers, video-only Compose layout and Activity mode forwarding.
Install the matching handler in APIs, then enter/exit. Back returns from fullscreen; PiP depends on OS/device support.
Android media controls
A real MediaSession bound to the current Player.
Enable Android media session, inspect app:media-session state, then test available system controls. Release it when finished.
Offline playback
SDK manager, track actions and loading the manager’s OfflineSourceConfig.
Create a manager, fetch/select download options, process them, wait for completion, then play downloaded source without networking.
Playlists, advertising, content protection and Cast
Typed SDK configuration and commands are available in the advanced panels.
Provide matching playlist/ad/DRM inputs or a configured Cast receiver. Inspect SDK events and actual playback, not just command success.

blocks.text: PiP displays a small video window above other apps. The Manifest enables it and MainActivity forwards onPictureInPictureModeChanged to active views, subject to OS/TV support. MediaSession connects the Player to Android system controls; Cast transfers playback to a receiver.

Offline managers use a stable content ID. Downloads may wait for all chosen device/network requirements, and each track action is selected explicitly. Releasing the manager keeps files; deleting content removes that ID’s cache.

Protected assets need rights, a license service and storage. Check license download/renew/release separately from media completion. The advanced offline source constructor neither imports SDK-managed downloads nor issues licenses. Use Play downloaded source for ordinary managed downloads so the SDK supplies matching cache and track metadata.

blocks.caption: After SDK processing, the audio track shows state=Downloaded, action=null, None selected and progress=100.0%. Choose track actions and use Process selected actions to submit them. Offline playback is checked separately.

blocks.text: Release the view and Player with their owners

Treat the Activity, PlayerView and Player as separate lifetimes. attachView forwards the Activity’s start, resume, pause and stop through PlayerViewLifecycle. The observer catches up a new view when the Activity is already resumed. Remove that observer before retiring a view. MainActivity.onDestroy calls controller.release to unsubscribe, release offline/media-session resources and destroy the Player. Do not replace this with repeatedly constructing the Player on resume.

blocks.title: Detach the shared Player before retiring its view
blocks.text:
internal fun releaseView(view: PlayerView) {
        if (!views.remove(view)) return
        retireApiViewSubscriptions(view)
        retireApiViewHandlers(view)
        apiSurfaces.clear(view)
        if (apiDetachedView === view) apiDetachedView = null
        viewLifecycle.detach(view)
        view.player = null
        view.onDestroy()
    }

PlayerController owns the Player, so releaseView sets view.player = null before view.onDestroy(). Otherwise retiring a view can also destroy the Player it still holds. This ordering is why changing the app’s UI mode can preserve playback. Controller release is idempotent and ultimately calls player.destroy(); keep the same ownership rule when adding fullscreen surfaces or other hosts.
Useful details and FAQ
blocks.summary: Investigate unapplied settings, playback resets, UI and subtitle issues, licensing, and lifecycle behavior through the applied code and SDK state.

blocks.title: Why did Apply not change the value I see?
blocks.text: First check which Apply action was used and whether validation succeeded. Player and source drafts are independent. SDK API overrides take precedence over the standard form, and staging Stage override still requires Apply SDK. Compare the standard applied code and the separate applied override code. A startup-only setting, such as SDK debug logging, shows a saved next-launch value; fully stop and reopen the app to activate it.

blocks.title: Why did my playback position reset?
blocks.text: Applying player or advanced SDK settings recreates the Player and reloads the source’s configured start offset. That path intentionally does not resume the old position. A UI-picker change alone replaces PlayerView while keeping the Player. If your integration loses playback during a view-only change, verify that it detaches the shared Player before destroying the old view and does not recreate Player during ordinary recomposition.

blocks.title: Why is my custom UI missing or unchanged?
blocks.text: Check the exact globally registered factory name, local asset paths and the applied PlayerViewConfig. Build the shared UI, synchronize its output, rebuild and reinstall the APK. supplementalCssLocation must point to an asset you packaged or a reachable resource; entering its name does not create the file. A factory exported only for Web is not automatically registered for the Android WebView.

blocks.title: Why are subtitles off or the requested language absent?
blocks.text: An external track’s isDefault flag is metadata and does not enable captions. Apply the source, inspect the track list and select the track. Audio priorities can only select languages present in the stream; a nonempty source list overrides the player list. Clear the source list to inherit player preferences. Check the subtitle URL, format and network accessibility before changing the UI.

blocks.title: Why does the buffer or bitrate differ from my expectation?
blocks.text: Buffer values describe media duration, not fixed loading delays or a process-memory limit. Automatic bitrate selection also depends on available renditions and observed conditions. maxSelectableVideoBitrate caps automatic selection, while manual selection can still choose higher qualities. Compare the actual selected quality and stall events with the same content and network before concluding that a config was ignored.

blocks.title: Why is a playback event absent from a view subscription?
blocks.text: PlayerView subscriptions handle view UI events. Observe Playing and seeking events on Player, and source loading/errors on Source. The Events panel records occurrence counts when Record SDK events is enabled; zero means no event was recorded, not that the API was unavailable. State values are refreshed separately.

blocks.title: What should I check for license or source errors?
blocks.text: For player authorization error 1003, verify the installed app’s actual application ID com.playerlab.android and the Player license’s Android allowlist, then synchronize the intended local configuration and rebuild the APK. For source failures, inspect the numeric SourceError and check URL reachability, stream format and content-protection requirements. The standard form accepts HTTP URLs, but the device’s cleartext-network policy can still reject them; prefer HTTPS. Do not infer a licensing cause from every playback error.

blocks.title: Why did foregrounding or a TV change the behavior?
blocks.text: Lifecycle forwarding does not guarantee automatic resumption. The recorded SDK 3.171.0 phone-emulator check remained paused after foregrounding. On TV, check focus, remote input and UI variant separately. Emulator results or a TV launcher declaration do not establish physical-device or Cast receiver playback.

items.label: Recorded test results and environment scope

blocks.text: Analytics / Observability
blocks.summary: Configure the bundled Analytics collector and content metadata, then locate the playback session and inspect its metrics in Bitmovin Dashboard Observability.

blocks.text: After Player and source behavior is working, configure the bundled Analytics collector to send playback events to your Bitmovin account. The Analytics license is separate from the Player license. The Android build reads its configured Analytics license through the manifest; an empty build key disables the default collector. An account API key is not an Analytics collection license and should not be placed in the app.
ApiAnalyticsSettings.playerConfig builds AnalyticsConfig and returns AnalyticsPlayerConfig.Enabled with DefaultMetadata, or Disabled. Pass it to the SDK Player constructor.

The panel offers Build key, Deferred license and Disabled. Apply Analytics recreates the Player. Without an override, Deferred license passes DEFERRED so the SDK fetches an enabled Analytics license associated with the Player license. Check collector state and the matching Dashboard session.

blocks.title: Attach content metadata through the Analytics SDK type

blocks.text: Pass SourceMetadata through AnalyticsSourceConfig.Enabled when creating a Source. Set a stable videoId and useful title before playback to find content in Dashboard. These are separate from SourceConfig.title used by the player UI.

Default metadata supports cdnProvider/customUserId; source metadata supports title/videoId/cdnProvider/path/isLive. Both support customData and experimentName. Use test identifiers without personal or confidential data.

items: Apply the Analytics license/mode and metadata, play a source and record the time, content identifier, app version and device.
Open Bitmovin Dashboard → Observability, select the matching Analytics license and a period containing the playback, then filter by content and device. Verify the Dashboard’s time zone.

Find the corresponding session and inspect startup, rebuffering, errors and playback information. Match session timing with the app’s SDK events. A local event count or enabled collector alone does not confirm Dashboard receipt.
For before/after comparisons, keep content, network, device, metric definition and filter scope consistent. Use the linked metric, query and visualization chapters for aggregated results.
